significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) law—that cross-lingual corruption "decays with typological and script distance" and is directionally stronger from high-resource languages—plus a form-(ii) mechanism in which a "compact set of shared concept-binding neurons" causally mediates that corruption. This fixes expected interference across many source-target pairs and informs the specificity assumptions behind multilingual transfer and model-editing work such as ECLeKTic (Hu et al., 2024), ROME, and MEMIT, rather than merely showing that a representation exists. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a causal mechanism; a negative result would still rule out language distance as a general predictor and/or compact shared-neuron mediation, although the composite claim permits mixed outcomes. The true and false states are distinguishable, and the topic-substitution check passes: the topic alone suggests studying shared versus language-specific representations, but not this specific directional distance law, resource asymmetry, and causal mediator.

reach.justification: The principal transferable handle is the claimed "quantitative interference-vs-distance model," supplemented by a "training-free intervention that reduces harmful spillover." The distance model is ex ante because it could forecast which source-target language pairs are vulnerable before a multilingual edit or contaminated context is deployed, giving model editors, auditors, and deployment teams an action window; the neuron intervention is instead model-calibrated mitigation after localization. After re-extraction on a new model, the asserted decay and resource-direction asymmetry still predict a qualitative relation, whereas the exact neurons would need rediscovery; the hypothesis is framed across multilingual LLMs, language families, scripts, and both contextual injection and parameter editing. The topic-substitution check passes because generic multilingual-representation research supplies neither this predictive contamination ledger nor its mitigation handle, so the reach comes from the claim rather than the topic.
